_comment: Machine-readable sibling to _template.md. scripts/fetch_updates.py reads exactly this shape via --config. Fill in every field for a new ecosystem; nothing here needs a skill-file edit. See dart-flutter.json for a filled-in example, and _template.md for the human-readable slot descriptions these fields correspond to (outdated_cmd -> outdated_cmd, registry_api -> registry_api, advisory_source -> advisory_source, changelog_convention -> changelog, version_scheme -> strip_build_suffix_regex).
ecosystem: <name matching the sibling .md file, e.g. dart-flutter>
outdated_shape: <which normalizer scripts/fetch_updates.py uses to parse outdated_cmd's stdout into its common internal shape -- one of: 'pub' (an object with a 'packages' array, each package's version fields nested as {"version": ...}, a 'kind' of 'direct'/'dev'), 'npm_style_object' (an object keyed by package name, each value carrying current/wanted/latest/dependencyType -- covers npm and pnpm, whose shapes match exactly), 'array_flat' (a flat array of {"name", "version", "latest_version"} objects, no wanted/dev-vs-direct distinction -- covers pip and uv), 'yarn_table' (Yarn Classic's {"type": "table", "data": {"head": [...], "body": [[...]]}} column-table envelope), 'poetry_array' (a flat array of {"name", "version", "latest"} objects -- unverified shape, see python-poetry.json's _note). A genuinely new shape needs a new normalizer function added to fetch_updates.py -- that's the one case adding an ecosystem still touches script code, since there's no way to parse an unknown JSON shape from config data alone.>
outdated_cmd: <argv list, e.g. ["fvm", "flutter", "pub", "outdated", "--json"] -- run via subprocess in the manifest directory, must produce JSON on stdout (a non-JSON banner prefix is tolerated -- the script skips to the first '{' or '[')>
sdk_placeholder_version: <optional. Some ecosystems report an SDK-constrained pseudo-package (e.g. Dart/Flutter's 'flutter'/'flutter_test' sdk: dependencies) with a sentinel version instead of a real one (pub uses "0.0.0"). Packages whose reported latest version equals this value are skipped entirely -- they have no real pub.dev-style version to audit, and the toolchain-audit skill owns the actual SDK version. Omit this field if the ecosystem has no such sentinel. Only meaningful for outdated_shape 'pub'.>
manifest_filename: <the manifest's filename within manifest_dir, e.g. "pubspec.yaml", "package.json", "requirements.txt", "pyproject.toml" -- used to compute the reported manifest path and to locate the file for the manifest-fallback version read. Defaults to "pubspec.yaml" if omitted, for backward compatibility -- always set this explicitly for a new ecosystem.>
manifest_version_pattern: <regex with a {name} placeholder and one capture group, used as a fallback to read the declared version straight out of the manifest file when outdated_cmd can't determine 'current' (e.g. a package with no lockfile). Applied line-by-line against the manifest (or against manifest_section_headers's scoped lines, if set).>
manifest_section_headers: <optional array of literal lines (e.g. ["dependencies:", "dev_dependencies:"]) that scope manifest_version_pattern's line-by-line search to just the lines inside one of these top-level sections -- prevents an unrelated section from accidentally matching the same package-name pattern. Omit (or set null) for a manifest format with no such literal section-header convention (JSON/TOML dependency blocks, a flat requirements.txt) -- the whole file gets scanned instead, which is fine since the regex itself is anchored on the package name.>
strip_build_suffix_regex: <regex matching a non-semver build suffix to strip before comparing versions, e.g. \+\d+$ for pub's +N suffix. Use an regex that never matches anything if the ecosystem has no such suffix.>

registry_api.url_template: <URL with a {name} placeholder returning that package's version list/metadata as JSON, e.g. https://pub.dev/api/packages/{name}>

advisory_source.ecosystem_name: <the OSV.dev ecosystem name for this package manager, e.g. Pub, npm, PyPI -- see https://ossf.github.io/osv-schema/#affectedpackage-field for the list>

changelog.url_template: <URL with a {name} placeholder for that package's changelog/release notes, e.g. https://pub.dev/packages/{name}/changelog>
changelog.version_header_regex: <regex with a {version} placeholder matching a changelog's per-version heading line, e.g. ^##\s+\[?v?{version}\]? for markdown '## 1.2.3' or '## [1.2.3]' style headers. If the ecosystem's changelog convention doesn't use a parseable heading pattern, the script falls back to 'could not parse, see changelog_url' rather than guessing.>
